A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Freqformer and are readable through their final references. Text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4–4.2 report original FHDMi/UHDM restoration results and experiments testing training strategies, frequency decomposition and architectural components.

after.justification: Sections 4–4.2 report original results on four datasets, additional comparator evaluations and expanded transform and architecture ablations.

M1.justification: The decomposition kernel, dual branches, SA-CA, hierarchical fusion, learnable FCT and two-stage losses remain unchanged. The explicit description of resized low-frequency inference resolves an inconsistent overview in v1; v1 Section 3.2 already specified small inputs during both training and inference.

E1.justification: TIP2018 and LCDMoire move from related-work discussion to actual training and evaluation, alongside retained FHDMi and UHDM experiments. This broadens coverage beyond high-resolution benchmarks to 256×256 natural-scene images and a synthetic, text-focused dataset. Adding adapted RAW/video comparator architectures does not establish evaluation on RAW or video datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds RRID and DTNet on FHDMi/UHDM and STD-Net on FHDMi. The ablations additionally introduce Block DCT and DAT comparisons. Conversely, v1 Table 5's dedicated comparison against ESDNet on separate frequency branches disappears, although ESDNet remains in other experiments.

E3.justification: Existing FHDMi/UHDM splits, metrics, crop/resize sizes and 150-epoch training stages are retained. Added experiments specify TIP2018's 135,000/15,000 training/test split and 256/256 crop/resize sizes, LCDMoire's 10,000/100 training/validation split and 512/512 sizes, and an 8×8 Block-DCT control. These extend the protocol without documenting a redesign of the original benchmark evaluations.

E4.justification: The transform analysis expands from one Haar experiment to quantitative Haar/DCT comparisons and qualitative artifact examples in Table 3 and Figure 7. Table 6 adds full-convolution SCP and DAT architecture controls. The separate branchwise ESDNet analysis is removed, while the resizing and learnable-FCT studies survive as renumbered Tables 4–5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The expanded results retain the same single-score reporting practice.

E6.justification: New benchmark results include TIP2018/LCDMoire PSNRs of 30.63/45.62, plus added comparator and ablation entries. Freqformer's UHDM PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS change from 22.22/0.8018/0.2434 to 22.24/0.8021/0.2424; FHDMi scores remain unchanged. Haar PSNR changes from 13.32 to 23.01, and Table 6 scores and timings are replaced without establishing identical conditions. Section 3.2's high-frequency resizing PSNR changes from approximately 30 to 25 dB. Section 4.1 adds 0.58 versus 0.25 s/image for Freqformer versus ESDNet-L and revises Freqformer's computation from 2.49 to 2.46 TFLOPs.

T1.justification: The mathematical method and losses are retained. The added equality expressing the high-frequency residual as the original image minus its low-frequency component restates the existing recurrence. No substantive new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central contributions and compact, state-of-the-art restoration claim remain. The abstract strengthens the comparative premise by attributing spatial discontinuity, channel redundancy and reconstruction errors to discrete Haar/block-DCT representations, extending v1's narrower discussion of underexploited wavelet approaches.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds explanations involving shift variance, secondary aliasing, block-DCT stationarity and channel redundancy. Section 4.1 newly qualifies the efficiency discussion: Freqformer has fewer FLOPs but slower inference than ESDNet-L, tentatively attributed to less optimized attention operations. The central texture/color interpretation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation information for new experiments, including the Haar variant's band-specific modules and 10.921M parameters, and clarifies inference. However, it omits v1's explicit initial learning rate of 0.0002. The abstract changes the code-availability statement from publicly available to a future release; the PDFs do not establish the repository's actual availability.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 broadens from wavelet-based to frequency-based methods, adding DCT positioning against MBCNN and FHDe2Net and revising the critique of FHDe2Net. STD-Net and generative-restoration references are added. The existing research lineage and principal novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: The section sequence and much of the method exposition remain, with localized rewrites, clearer inference wording and reordered ablation discussion. The title changes 'Efficient' to 'Effective,' asymmetric training terminology becomes more prominent, author/affiliation information changes, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different template with narrower text, running headers and substantially reorganized displays. New Figures 3 and 7 illustrate transform differences and ablation outputs. Tables 1, 2 and 6 expand; the old branch-comparison table disappears. Ablation tables move from text-wrapped placements to full-width blocks, and qualitative comparisons replace a UHDM example and introduce RRID panels.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central design: the expanded Haar/DCT study and new SCP/DAT controls test choices that v1 supported only narrowly. Distinct additional datasets and comparator families strengthen the generality assessment, while measured latency makes the efficiency discussion more candid. These gains outweigh the removed branch comparison, omitted learning rate and less definite code-release statement. Unexplained changes to existing ablation scores and timings remain a reproducibility limitation.
